This. Representation is a resource, if it wasn't people would not invest other resources into acquiring it. Now think in tems of supply and demand. Expanding the domain of representation (the globalist direction) decreases the number of "suppliers" of representation.
>Bigger states = Fewer states
If there is no shared interests or identity, going from a world in which each group has their own state, to a world in which both groups "share" a state doesn't create solidarity, it creates conflict, as these groups are the "consumers" of representation. By reducing the supply of representation, you neccessarily create additional competition on the demand side. The fact that competition on the demand side benefits the supply side should be a major clue as to why the elite is always in favor of globalism.

If the people share a common identity, this is kind of like "reducing demand", so shared identity can allow for bigger states, but the question still remains. Why? And why not apply the same logic in other domains? Would two neighbours be better off sharing a house, just because they get along? Would the entire street be better off sharing a really big house? Uniting two states in which the people share common identity and solidarity still reduces the representation supply. The only advantage I can see is to international businesses, who are inconvenienced by borders, and for military organization in the event or war, and the only people I ever see demanding the merger of nation states for practical, non ideological reasons are business and military leaders.
